A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original hidden-state alignment, emotion probing, multilingual steering, and component-ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, and adds English/non-English aggregate comparisons.

M1.justification: The centered-SVD subspace, emotion-dependent layer selection, residual GELU steering module, and token, margin, and semantic losses are unchanged. Expanded methodological descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic corpus, eight human-written emotion datasets, and GSM8K control. English/non-English grouping and discussion of Hindi and German distribution shifts reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: The same LLaMA, OLMo, and Ministral comparisons, unsteered reference outputs, and ablated variants remain. No cited steering approach becomes a newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported metric specification changes: v1 Section 4.2 treats ℓ2-distortion near 1 as ideal, whereas v2 Section 3 describes squared deviations from a global scale with ideal 0. Retained experimental settings and per-dataset values are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that this revision involved recomputation.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit English/non-English subgroup comparisons addressing differences in geometric alignment and steering effectiveness. The GSM8K control, cross-model analyses, and all steering ablations already appear in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: The existing means, dispersion reporting, and plot legends remain, with the same reporting practice applied to the new aggregate rows. Neither version provides additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds language-group result entries and replaces v1's pooled alignment summary with grouped summaries. For example, v2 Table 2 reports OLMo steering from 11% to 91% for English and 11% to 86% for non-English. Matched per-dataset geometry and steering tables, correlation tables, and ablation values are unchanged; these additions do not establish performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V2 revises the stated mathematical characterization of ℓ2-distortion, changing its ideal from approximately 1 to 0 and describing deviations from a global scale. The added least-squares and stress equations otherwise explain existing calculations; no new theorem, proof, or steering-loss derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and three listed contributions are unchanged. However, v2's conclusion explicitly conditions the central universality claim on languages and styles being reasonably represented in pretraining, narrowing its stated applicability.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes directional universality from strict isometry and expands interpretations of language-group differences and limited pretraining coverage. It also adds intended-use discussion and an untested assertion that steering cannot induce or amplify harmful content beyond the base model's permissions.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly documents regression over same-emotion activations, distance and stretch calculations, and selection of distortion thresholds from the model/dataset distribution. Section 4.1 clarifies the synthetic and human-written datasets' roles. These are additional disclosures; the steering implementation and stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chennuru Vankadara and von Luxburg's 2018 work on distortion measures. The remaining cited works and substantive positioning against prior emotion-representation and steering research are retained.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands and reorganizes Methods, combines the former universality, model-psychology, and steering sections under Experiments, and rewrites the results narrative around language-group comparisons. It also adds limitations and ethics paragraphs and reorganizes the appendices around relocated detailed results.

P2.justification: The main evidence displays are substantially reorganized: v2 Tables 1–2 summarize English/non-English groups, combining or replacing earlier main-text summaries. V1's large per-dataset Tables 1 and 3 move to appendix Tables 5 and 8. The plots and other numerical tables are retained but repositioned and reflowed.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing study easier to assess through expanded methodological explanations, language-group summaries that retain detailed appendix results, and explicit qualifications of universality. The gain is limited: the empirical evidence is essentially unchanged, the revised ℓ2-distortion ideal is not reconciled with retained results, and the new categorical safety assurance lacks supporting evaluation. These issues constrain an otherwise modest improvement in exposition and scope qualification.
